answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to stake a small refundable deposit before joining the economy, with the stake slashed if peers catch duplicate identities. Like stars emerging from a nebula at dawn, genuine agents accumulate a verifiable history of useful work across the open meadow of shared tasks, while cheap sock-puppet accounts cannot afford to stake and behave honestly at scale. Reputation earned over time, not claimed at signup, makes sybil attacks expensive and easy to spot.
